title: Bound a teacher-built practice tool to a visible ruleset
source_observation: The lecturer moved AI upstream: it helped build a deterministic student applet rather than directly generating student-facing questions. He first requested a plan and clarification, then corrected visual and data-structure errors with concrete examples and tested early versions.
requires: A task with explicit rules and answer conditions
A teacher able to inspect examples and test revisions
A reversible practice surface
excludes: Open-ended content where correctness cannot be checked
Treating the generated applet as validated learning evidence
unknowns: Student uptake and learning gains were not reported
Accessibility and maintenance beyond the reported Canvas integration
method_steps: Specify the task and what the tool must not do
Ask the model to restate the plan and surface questions
Prototype, test a few cases, and report concrete errors
Revise the bounded data representation and interface
Keep teacher review before exposing the tool to students
proposed_followup: Observe which generated practice items students attempt, abandon, or ask about, and sample answer validity before revising the generator.
transfer_note: For cMOOC use, this supports a teacher-approved resource-building candidate when an activity has explicit state and answer rules. It does not establish automated facilitation or a learning effect.

title: Use reference texts to compare multiple situated renderings
source_observation: The practitioner uploaded reference texts and used carefully structured prompts to generate translations in different dialects, idioms, and historically appropriate styles, treating translation as creative negotiation rather than a single equivalent answer.
requires: Teacher-selected source texts and language context
A learning task that values comparison and interpretation
Human discussion of cultural and representational choices
excludes: Assuming the model preserves cultural meaning automatically
Using output as an authoritative translation without review
unknowns: Detailed classroom sequence and learner outcomes were not reported
How different language communities judged the outputs
method_steps: Choose a text and make the intended linguistic or cultural variation explicit
Provide a small reference corpus
Ask for several deliberately different renderings
Compare choices against the source and discuss whose voice is represented
Record unresolved translation decisions
proposed_followup: Ask participants to annotate where versions diverge and whether the divergence opens a question for peers rather than closes interpretation.
transfer_note: A cMOOC analogue could use variant AI renderings as discussion prompts for perspective-taking, while keeping cultural interpretation and any public response with learners and teachers.

title: Ask AI to stress-test a teacher-owned session plan
source_observation: The teacher supplied his own objectives, audience, and conceptual drafts, then asked AI to identify gaps, ambiguities, assumptions, counter-positions, and scenario prompts. He used NotebookLM for alternative audio access to selected readings and retained academic review of the outputs.
requires: Teacher-owned source material and learning outcomes
A clear audience and desired critical stance
Time for teacher verification and revision
excludes: Asking AI to originate disciplinary content without source control
Treating audio summaries as substitutes for core readings
unknowns: The reported drafting-time reduction was a practitioner estimate
No controlled comparison of session quality was provided
method_steps: State audience, goals, and disciplinary boundary
Ask for coherence checks and counter-positions
Select only useful questions or scenarios
Convert curated material into an optional alternate format
Re-read and edit against the learning outcomes
proposed_followup: After the session, record which AI-raised questions changed the activity and which were rejected by the teacher.
transfer_note: This can inform a cMOOC teacher-facing reflection prompt, but it should remain a draft-support and critique aid rather than an autonomous course judgement.

title: Turn correction into guided self-editing
source_observation: The translation coach points learners to grammar references, highlights issues, asks questions, and suggests follow-up exercises. The teacher explicitly reports the trust problem that learners may not know whether an AI explanation is correct before they have mastered the answer.
requires: A bounded reference set such as grammar rules and model answers
A task where questioning supports self-editing
Teacher and learner routes for verification
excludes: Directly accepting an AI correction as authoritative
Assuming additional AI practice is cost-free in tutorial time
unknowns: No independent comparison with teacher feedback was reported
The extent of student use was not quantified
method_steps: Define the target skill and reference material
Configure the tool to ask before suggesting
Require the learner to explain or revise a choice
Point to the source rule or example
Escalate uncertainty to a tutor or peer
proposed_followup: Track repeated questions and disagreement cases to identify where the reference set or teacher explanation needs repair.
transfer_note: For cMOOC facilitation, the pattern supports question-first peer revision and explicit teacher handoff; it does not support silently correcting community contributions.

title: Pair AI practice with explicit critical checking
source_observation: The course combined guided Socratic questioning, self-quizzing, and deliberate error detection instead of answer delivery. Tutors first developed subject-specific ability to judge the tool's accuracy and then discussed responsible use with students.
requires: Clear concepts and course-level learning goals
Tutors who can judge typical errors
A safe space to compare scepticism and over-reliance
excludes: AI-generated answers as a replacement for demonstrated student ability
General claims that balanced attitudes prove learning
unknowns: No control group or long-term retention measure was reported
Exact prompts and tutor workload were not supplied
method_steps: Identify a concept students must reason through
Use a question-first tutor mode
Generate low-stakes self-checks
Present plausible but flawed text for diagnosis
Discuss the limits and require independent assessment evidence
proposed_followup: Observe whether learners explain the error or merely accept the tutor's correction, then adjust the prompt and teacher debrief.
transfer_note: This provides a candidate pattern for cMOOC claim checking and peer questioning; it cannot be treated as evidence that an AI tutor improves community learning.

title: Offer an alternate preparation route with a discussion return
source_observation: The podcast was treated as a second source rather than a replacement for the paper. Students used it to recover details before discussion, while the team noticed that positive tone and missing nuance needed correction.
requires: Curated readings and a clear reason for the alternate format
A teacher or tutor who can check tone and nuance
A follow-up discussion connected to the original text
excludes: Presenting an AI summary as the whole reading
Assuming confidence or engagement equals comprehension
unknowns: No controlled learning outcome was reported
Accessibility benefits may differ by learner and language
method_steps: Select a bounded reading set
Generate a dialogue-style summary
Check scientific claims and tone
Label it as an additional preparation aid
Ask learners to bring one supported question to discussion
proposed_followup: Compare questions raised from the original reading and audio aid, and record where the audio omitted or distorted nuance.
transfer_note: A cMOOC version could offer optional audio orientation to a dense thread, but replies should remain grounded in the source and learner interpretation.

title: Treat a failed automation pilot as a boundary on use
source_observation: The team tested an apparently routine feedback-analysis task and found that quality assurance and contextual interpretation outweighed the hoped-for administrative savings. It retained narrower summary and presentation possibilities while rejecting primary analysis of complex feedback.
requires: A defined feedback workflow and a way to compare workload
Human reviewers who understand course context
Permission to stop or narrow a pilot
excludes: Calling an attempted pilot an effective feedback loop
Using AI to infer student meaning from raw comments without review
unknowns: Exact prompt versions and workload counts were not published
The result may differ with other models or pre-processing
method_steps: Define the intended task and quality standard
Run a small bounded pilot
Record prompting, interpretation, and checking effort
Compare with the existing process
Narrow or discontinue the use if context costs dominate
proposed_followup: For any cMOOC feedback candidate, log time, disagreement, and unresolved context rather than only counting generated summaries.
transfer_note: This is a cautionary method card: a failed efficiency hypothesis is useful boundary evidence and does not justify automatic sentiment or activity interpretation.

title: Keep a course helper inside a known information boundary
source_observation: The team iterated across platforms, tested with staff and students, and found that a small data pool caused unsupported answers. The design lesson was to scope the bot and make uncertainty explicit instead of inventing a course fact.
requires: A maintained, authoritative course information set
A clear user-facing scope and fallback
Testing by people who know the course
excludes: Using a helper to answer beyond its indexed materials
Interpreting positive tone as factual reliability
unknowns: No public accuracy rate or maintenance schedule was given
The reported rollout status may change
method_steps: Map the information currently scattered across locations
Choose the smallest useful source set
Test known and unknown questions
Add an explicit uncertainty response
Embed the helper in the existing learning surface and re-test after updates
proposed_followup: Collect unanswered and corrected questions as maintenance candidates, preserving the course/version context for each correction.
transfer_note: For cMOOC use, the pattern supports a bounded orientation helper over course manifests; it does not authorize the helper to infer participant state or make facilitation decisions.

title: Design role-play around scenario-specific responses and replay
source_observation: The project combined a realistic role with replay, repetition, reflection, and automated feedback. The teaching value depended on clear instructions and scenario design; realistic resistance was a known weakness.
requires: A bounded fictional scenario and explicit learning goal
A psychologically safe practice setting
Human review of scenario and feedback quality
excludes: Using model behaviour as a clinically authoritative patient representation
Assuming a cooperative dialogue covers the full skill range
unknowns: No comparative performance evidence was reported
The reliability of automated feedback across cases is unknown
method_steps: Define what the learner must practise
Specify what information the role should reveal and when
Include a replay or transcript for reflection
Test cooperative and resistant variants
Have an instructor debrief errors and limitations
proposed_followup: Record which scenario turns prompt learners to seek help, revise their approach, or abandon the interaction.
transfer_note: A cMOOC analogue could use fictional stakeholder roles to rehearse dialogue, with human moderation retaining responsibility for interpretation and safety.

title: Let teachers validate multiple access formats before sharing
source_observation: The workflow starts from educator-owned materials, generates several modes, and keeps subject experts as the faithfulness check. It aims to add access without making every lecturer author each format manually.
requires: Stable teacher-owned content
Known accessibility purposes and learner choices
A teacher review step for each format
excludes: Offering all formats as equally accurate without review
Assuming multimodality alone solves access barriers
unknowns: No detailed fidelity error log was reported
Long-term workload and adoption after scaling are unknown
method_steps: Identify a material and access barrier
Generate a small set of alternate formats
Check terminology, emphasis, and omissions
Offer choices without forcing one route
Collect learner requests and revise the workflow
proposed_followup: Log which format choices lead to questions or corrections, and return those issues to the teacher rather than silently regenerating.
transfer_note: For cMOOC, this supports optional summaries or audio entry points over teacher-approved material; it does not convert learner contributions into public content automatically.

title: Make optional voice practice reviewable and scenario-bound
source_observation: The tool combined extended conversation with transcripts so learners could review what they said. Teachers explored transfer across languages, while the project kept opt-out choice and meaningful scenarios as design requirements.
requires: A target language and scenario with a communicative purpose
Transcript or other reflection support
An opt-out path and teacher involvement
excludes: Forcing all learners into one AI speaking route
Using generic verbose dialogue as evidence of language progress
unknowns: No controlled oral proficiency result was reported
The accuracy of speech feedback across accents is unknown
method_steps: Define a realistic scenario
Set a concise response style
Offer a short conversation and transcript
Ask the learner to mark one successful and one uncertain turn
Discuss or revise the scenario with a teacher
proposed_followup: Observe whether transcript review leads to learner-initiated revision or peer exchange, and capture reasons for opting out.
transfer_note: A cMOOC version could support optional rehearsal of a contribution or facilitation phrase, while preserving human-to-human exchange as the primary interaction.

title: Use AI feedback to generate discussion and reflection
source_observation: The tool was deliberately designed to point out issues and contextualise them without supplying a finished correction. The reported value lay in immediate revision and classroom conversation, not replacement of human teaching.
requires: A reference-aware language task
A teacher-defined feedback purpose
A revision or discussion step after the AI response
excludes: Treating immediate feedback as final correctness
Using the prototype as an unsupervised self-study authority
unknowns: The page does not provide error rates or a comparison with tutor feedback
Usability issues were not itemised
method_steps: Set the target passage and language context
Ask the tool to identify and explain an issue
Have the learner propose a revision
Compare with a reference or peer explanation
Use unresolved cases for teacher-led discussion
proposed_followup: Collect correction disagreements and the learner's reasoning as revision evidence rather than measuring only the corrected sentence.
transfer_note: For cMOOC writing support, the pattern favours prompts that elicit reasoning and peer response instead of auto-editing a post.

title: Place AI between a contribution and a peer conversation
source_observation: The project used AI to produce questions from written work, then directed those questions toward face-to-face interdisciplinary discussion. The in-class demonstration and whole-group feedback were part of the pilot design.
requires: A contribution that participants have permission to discuss
A real peer conversation after prompt generation
Human control over question relevance and sensitivity
excludes: Letting AI replace the dialogue it is meant to support
Inferring a participant's intention from text alone
unknowns: No evidence of sustained community outcomes was reported
The platform's question quality was not quantified
method_steps: Select a bounded contribution
Generate a small set of comparison or clarification prompts
Let peers choose which question to pursue
Record responses and unresolved differences
Use feedback to refine prompt types
proposed_followup: Observe whether the generated prompts lead to reciprocal replies, substantive revision, or only short agreement.
transfer_note: This is a strong cMOOC candidate for preserving peer opportunity: a possible prompt may open a conversation, but the system should not answer on behalf of participants.

title: Expose the checklist and invite learners to repair it
source_observation: AI output was shown alongside a structured checklist and its reasoning. Student codesign feedback changed the granularity of checklist items so evaluation could be more precise.
requires: An explicit evaluative checklist
Source material that learners may inspect
A route for student feedback to change the tool
excludes: Opaque AI scores treated as evidence of reproducibility
A checklist that hides disciplinary disagreement
unknowns: No agreement rate against expert reviewers was reported
The educational effect of showing reasoning remains open
method_steps: Define the human evaluation standard
Ask AI to map evidence to each item
Show source location and uncertainty
Invite learners to challenge the mapping
Revise checklist granularity from observed difficulties
proposed_followup: Record which checklist items generate the most peer disagreement and whether the disagreement leads to better evidence requests.
transfer_note: For cMOOC, this supports transparent evidence prompts and teacher review, but AI explanations remain candidate reasoning rather than authoritative verification.

title: Orient inquiry with sources while blocking answer substitution
source_observation: The tool narrowed an overwhelming topic into contextual reading pathways and explicitly aimed not to produce complete essay solutions. Evaluator feedback identified dataset coverage and outline-generation risks, leading to a call for clearer guardrails and departmental discussion.
requires: A curated source collection with provenance
A topic where orientation is a real bottleneck
A teacher-defined boundary between guidance and completion
excludes: Using summaries without opening or checking the underlying texts
